title: The Clive Operating System
abstract: Clive is an operating system aimed at providing simple and high performance construction of network and cloud services. Currently it is used hosted on other systems to support further development of the system. In the future it will also run on native blades. Clive introduces new file system technology and novel interfaces for the construction of networked system.
summary: The paper appears to have had modest but identifiable influence within research on language-oriented operating systems, network file systems, and unikernels. Subsequent Clive-related work developed the system’s structured I/O framework and the ZX network file system, explicitly building on the Clive architecture. ([lsub.org](https://lsub.org/books-papers/)) The Clive operating system was also cited in later work on unikernel and library-operating-system designs, including GopherOS, RustyHermit, and research discussing the evolution from containers toward unikernels. ([usenix.org](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/osdi18-cutler.pdf)) Contemporary technical coverage presented Clive as a Go-based operating system influenced by Plan 9 and Nix, with the ZX protocol as a central design element. ([osnews.com](https://www.osnews.com/story/27747/clive-new-operating-system-based-on-plan-9-design/)) The available evidence indicates research and conceptual influence rather than substantial documented industrial adoption.
